claim: What matters more than anything is happiness, yours and what you bring others: "that's the only thing that matters", that and making memories
Stuff, being in shape, a good sex life, awesome kids, the trappings of the modern world are nice, but nothing else matters but your happiness
Miserable in a job that pays for your lifestyle, or unhappy in a relationship you're not brave enough to end: is that pursuing happiness in a way that feels true on the deepest level? Maybe not
Knocking out a job, relationship or habit that isn't contributing to our happiness sometimes takes bravery
Happiness is not easy: long-term happiness is not doing whatever feels good in the moment, and a lot of times it's the opposite
Sleeping in and sitting around all day might feel good in the moment, but leaves you feeling worse and worse the longer you do it
Not facing what you need to face in a relationship leaves you more and more unhappy
Job hunting or building a business to escape an unhappy job might not feel good, but it's what long-term happiness takes
Happiness is the measure, the ultimate measure of any alpha male, not the stuff, the people you know or the money
Only you know, within your own life and mind, how to be the most happy and bring the most happiness to others
Part of why we're here, and seemingly a huge role of our job as men: bringing happiness to those we love, our family, which sometimes means the hard short-term thing
If your family is missing the hell out of you because you're gone all the time at a job you hate, do something about it
Miserable because you're out of shape? Prioritize your long-term happiness
The more true joy lies behind something, most often the more resistance you'll face getting to it
Either we accept facing resistance over and over and move towards what holds true joy anyway, or we let resistance stand in the way and die with regret: be brave
Years, in so many different areas, were spent unhappy from not being willing to face resistance and pursue happiness
Happiness doesn't just happen
We choose to be happy kind of moment to moment, it seems: no matter how bad things are, we can always kind of choose our attitude
Long-term happiness is up to us too: choosing a path that creates happiness for us and others, the only thing we'll take with us
You could die where you stand, in the fractions of a second after getting hit by a bus
Pursuing our true happiness, as the guidepost and measure of our path, is the way to a life without regret
Deep joy comes a lot of times from harder short-term choices that aren't necessarily the easy choice

We all, it seems, have some aspect of our life we know inherently we truly want to change, for a different level of joy and satisfaction for us and maybe those around us, but we let resistance stand in the way
Choose happiness, and go after whatever is eating at you

The 15 minutes talked about a couple of days ago: every day, 15 minutes toward what will bring the greatest increase in joy for you and those around you, like submitting job applications, planning and building your own business, or setting a timer to talk and figure stuff out in a relationship
Really fit but miserable? Who cares
In fitness, a job or a relationship, "quote unquote success" without true happiness on a deep core level is failure, not success
You have more resistance-facing power than you've ever felt before
Today, take some positive step in an area of your life where you haven't been: figure out what holds you back from the most happiness and get after changing it
